chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: Kelly's Stables: everyone in a tiny room, nobody paid
summary: Hawkins, Billy Daniels and Nat Cole all played Kelly's Stables for about $100 a week; Kirby's band eventually earned a little.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Mildred Bailey was on 52nd Street then, and at Kelly's Stables -- I remember once at Kelly's Stables Coleman Hawkins was in there; Billy Daniels -- all at the same time -- Billy Daniels was in there; Nat Cole trio was in there. And who else was in there? Some singer -- I can't think who was in, some girl.
But all of them were in there, and another thing, I don't think any of them made over about 100 bucks a week, and all of them were in that -- in Kelly's Stables that one time.
Was Kelly's Stable that small also?
It was small, yes, very small. Frankie Newton had a little band. He's a trumpet player down there. Flip Phillips was his saxophone player --
Flip just wanted to work in that room because Hawk was working

in there, you know. But these are the days when -- nobody really made any money. Nat Cole was in it, playing intermissions down there with his little group, didn't make anything. Nobody -- money's just something you didn't -- you couldn't make, so you didn't even think about it. You just played because you loved to play back at that time, you know.

Every once in a while a guy would break loose and do a little something and make a little something for himself. Kirby -- I think that band finally did get to making a little money, not a lot, John Kirby's band, because they caught on on recordings after a while around, and that was after Maxine Sullivan started singing with them, you know, because Kirby was married to her at one time. John Kirby was married to her.
